nodes.title: In every world, a learning agent clearly beats both random play and a simple hand-written rule.
I can watch any trained agent play in a replay, and compare it with earlier points in training.
For every world, I can explain in my own words why its learning method works and where it struggles.
Each new world reuses one shared core (world interface, training loop, logging, replay viewer) instead of starting over.
A world starts a new episode from a seed, and the same seed always gives the same starting state.

criteria: Given a world and seed 42, when two episodes are started, then both starting states are identical.

nodes.title: Given the same seed and the same sequence of actions, a world produces the same sequence of observations, rewards and end signals.

criteria: Given a recorded episode's seed and actions, when they are replayed into a fresh world, then every observation, reward and end signal matches the recording.

nodes.title: Each agent's observation is a fixed-length list of numbers, never an image.

criteria: Given any world, when an observation is taken at any step, then it has the same length as at every other step of that world and variant.

nodes.title: A world declares its agents, the observation length and the action format (a choice from a fixed set, or a list of numbers within stated limits) before any episode starts.

criteria: Given any world, when the training loop asks for its description, then it receives the agent list, observation length and action format without running an episode.

nodes.title: Every world reports a per-episode score with a stated direction (higher is better, or lower is better), used by evaluation and charts.

criteria: Given a finished episode, when its score is requested, then a single number and the world's direction are returned.

nodes.title: A world reports its drawable state at every step (positions, sizes and kinds of every object) for the replay viewer.

criteria: Given any step of any episode, when the drawable state is requested, then every object on screen is listed with its position.

nodes.title: A world can hold more than one agent, each agent belonging to a named team.

criteria: Given a world with agents on two teams, when a step is taken, then each agent receives its own observation and reward, labelled with its team.

nodes.title: A training run is started from a world, a variant, the method's settings and a seed, and runs for a stated budget of environment steps.

criteria: Given snake, its default settings, seed 1 and a budget of N steps, when the run is started, then it stops after exactly N environment steps.

nodes.title: The same world, settings and seed on the same machine give an identical training run.

criteria: Given two runs with identical inputs, when both finish, then their logged results and final checkpoints are identical.

nodes.title: A run saves a checkpoint at every 10% of its budget, from the start (untrained) to the end.

criteria: Given a finished run, when its checkpoints are listed, then there are 11, at 0%, 10%, … 100% of the budget.

nodes.title: A run evaluates its current agent at every 5% of its budget on 20 episodes whose seeds are never used in training.

criteria: Given a finished run, when its evaluation log is read, then there are 21 evaluation points, each the mean score of 20 held-out-seed episodes.

nodes.title: Several runs of the same world with different seeds can be started together, one per processor core.

criteria: Given 5 seeds, when a batch of runs is started, then 5 runs proceed at the same time and each finishes with its own log and checkpoints.

nodes.title: Every learning method, before it is used in a world, learns the known best behavior in a tiny check world whose best behavior is worked out by hand.

criteria: Given a learning method and its check world, when it is trained for the check budget, then the trained agent picks the hand-derived best action in at least 95% of check-world states.

nodes.title: In worlds with more than one team, each team has its own learning method and settings, and all teams learn during the same run.

criteria: Given predator-prey with a learning method for each team, when a run proceeds, then both teams' agents change between consecutive checkpoints.

nodes.title: Every run records its world, variant, method settings, seed, budget, start and end times, and whether it finished.

criteria: Given any finished run, when its record is opened, then every one of those fields is present.

nodes.title: Every run logs, for each training episode, the episode's score, length and total reward per team.

criteria: Given a finished run, when its episode log is read, then it has one entry per training episode with those values.

nodes.title: For a world and variant with at least 3 finished runs, a learning-curve chart shows evaluation score against environment steps: the mean across runs as a line, the lowest-to-highest range across runs as a band, and each baseline's mean score as a horizontal reference line.

criteria: Given 5 finished snake runs, when the chart is made, then it shows one mean line, one band, a random-play line and a rule-based line, with the axes labelled with the score name and "environment steps".

nodes.title: Learning-curve charts follow the dataviz skill's guidance for form, colour and labelling.

criteria: Given any learning-curve chart, when it is reviewed against the dataviz skill, then it passes that skill's checks.

nodes.title: Each world can add its own logged measures (e.g. snake length at death, hits per fish), which are charted the same way as the score.

criteria: Given a world that declares an extra measure, when its chart is requested, then it is drawn with the same mean line and range band.

nodes.title: The learner can view the latest logged values of a run while it trains.

criteria: Given a run in progress, when the learner checks it, then they see the current step, the latest evaluation score and the time elapsed, no more than 1 evaluation point behind.

nodes.title: The learner can watch an episode played by any checkpoint of any run, from a seed they choose.

criteria: Given a snake run's 50% checkpoint and seed 7, when the replay is opened, then the episode plays from its first step to its end.

nodes.title: Replays are exact: the same checkpoint and seed always show the same episode.

criteria: Given a checkpoint and seed, when the replay is played twice, then every frame matches.

nodes.title: The replay can be paused, stepped one step forward or back, and played at 0.25×, 1×, 4× or 16× speed.

criteria: Given a paused replay at step 30, when the learner steps forward, then step 31 is shown; when they step back twice, step 29 is shown.

nodes.title: Two checkpoints can be shown side by side on the same starting state, stepping in sync.

criteria: Given the 10% and 100% snake checkpoints and seed 7, when compared, then both start from the same board and advance one step at a time together; when one episode ends, its last frame stays while the other continues.

nodes.title: The replay shows the current step, the running score and each agent's latest reward next to the world.

criteria: Given any frame, when it is shown, then the step number, the score so far and the latest rewards are visible.

nodes.title: The learner can also watch the random-play and rule-based baselines in the same viewer, including side by side with a checkpoint.

criteria: Given the rule-based snake and the final checkpoint on seed 7, when compared, then both play side by side as in REPLAY-04.

nodes.title: A replay can be saved as a video file to keep alongside the write-up.

criteria: Given an open replay, when the learner saves it, then a video of the whole episode at 1× speed is written and plays in a standard video player.

nodes.title: In worlds where agents see only nearby things, the replay can show each agent's sight radius as an overlay, switched on or off by the learner.

criteria: Given a local-sight fish replay, when the overlay is switched on, then a circle of the sight radius is drawn around every fish; when switched off, the circles disappear.

nodes.title: Every world and variant has a random-play baseline that picks each action uniformly from the allowed actions.

criteria: Given any world, when the random baseline plays 100 steps, then every action it takes is within the declared action format.

nodes.title: Every world and variant has a rule-based baseline that the learner writes by hand, described in one sentence in the world's feature below.

criteria: Given any world, when its rule baseline is listed, then its one-sentence description is shown with it.

nodes.title: Final evaluation plays every final checkpoint and both baselines on the same 100 seeds, none of which was used in training or in-training evaluation.

criteria: Given 5 finished runs, when final evaluation is run, then 700 episodes are played (5 × 100 learned, 100 random, 100 rule-based), all on the same 100 held-out seeds.

nodes.title: Whether the learned agent beats each baseline is tested with the null-hypothesis-testing skill. It is given: the hypothesis "the trained agent scores better than the baseline"; H0 = the learned agent's mean score is no better than the baseline's, H1 = it is better (in the world's score direction); the statistic = difference in mean episode score, learned (averaged over the runs, per seed) minus baseline; the null built by randomly swapping the learned and baseline labels within each held-out seed (paired permutation, 10,000 permutations); α = 0.05 with Holm correction across all baseline comparisons in that world (2 per variant); the EVAL-03 held-out episodes. The learned agent passes only if both nulls are rejected.

criteria: Given final evaluation results for one variant, when tested, then a report shows, for each baseline, the mean scores, the difference, the corrected p-value and reject/keep.

nodes.title: "Clearly beats" also needs every single run to beat the rule baseline: each run's final mean score is better than the rule-based baseline's mean score.

criteria: Given 5 runs where 4 beat the rule baseline and 1 does not, when the verdict is made, then the world is marked "not yet beating the baselines" and names the failing run.

nodes.title: Final evaluation produces one summary per world and variant: mean and range of learned scores across runs, both baseline means, the EVAL-04 test results and the EVAL-05 verdict.

criteria: Given a finished evaluation, when the summary is opened, then all of those values are present.

nodes.title: The learning algorithms (how actions are chosen, what is learned from each experience, and how the agent is updated) are written by the learner; automatic gradient computation may be used, but an established reference implementation of a learning method is used only for this check, never inside training runs.

criteria: Given any training run, when it runs, then no outside reinforcement-learning code takes part in it.

nodes.title: For each world and variant, 5 runs of a reference implementation of the same kind of method are trained on the same world, budget and seeds as the hand-written method, and evaluated as in EVAL-03.

criteria: Given a finished reference check, when its summary is opened, then it shows the reference's mean and range next to the hand-written method's.

nodes.title: The hand-written method passes the check if its mean final score is at least 80% of the reference's (or at most 125% for lower-is-better scores).

criteria: Given a hand-written snake mean of 18 food and a reference mean of 20, when checked, then it passes; at 15 against 20, it is flagged for investigation.

nodes.title: Each world has a write-up with three parts: how the learning method works, why it works in this world, and where it struggles.

criteria: Given a finished world, when its write-up is opened, then all three parts are present and non-empty.

nodes.title: The "where it struggles" part points to at least one saved replay or chart that shows the struggle.

criteria: Given a write-up, when its struggle part is read, then it names at least one saved replay or chart that exists.

nodes.title: Write-ups are the learner's own words; nothing in the system writes or fills them in.

criteria: Given a new world, when it is set up, then its write-up starts with only the three part headings.

nodes.title: The world is a 10 × 10 grid with one snake starting 3 cells long in the middle, and one food item on a random free cell.

criteria: Given seed 3, when an episode starts, then the snake is 3 cells long near the center and one food item is on a cell the snake does not cover.

nodes.title: Each step the snake chooses one of three actions: turn left, turn right or go straight.

criteria: Given the snake heading up, when it turns left, then its head moves one cell left.

nodes.title: Eating food grows the snake by one cell, adds 1 to the score and places new food on a random free cell.

criteria: Given the head moves onto food, when the step ends, then the snake is one cell longer, the score is up by 1 and new food is on a free cell.

nodes.title: The episode ends when the head hits a wall or the snake's body, or after 100 steps without eating.

criteria: Given the head moves into its own body, when the step ends, then the episode is over.

nodes.title: The score is the food eaten in the episode (higher is better).

criteria: Given an episode where 12 food items were eaten, when it ends, then its score is 12.

nodes.title: The snake observes a fixed list of numbers: danger straight ahead, left and right; its heading; the food's direction relative to its head; and its length.

criteria: Given any step, when the observation is taken, then it has the same length and holds those values.

nodes.title: The rule-based baseline moves toward the food along the shorter axis, unless that move would end the episode next step, in which case it takes any move that does not.

criteria: Given the food to the right and a free cell to the right, when the rule acts, then it moves right.

nodes.title: The trained snake beats both baselines as in EVAL-04 and EVAL-05.

criteria: Given 5 finished snake runs, when evaluated, then both baselines are beaten.

nodes.title: The tank is a square with walls; the ball moves in straight lines at constant speed and bounces off walls.

criteria: Given the ball heading into the right wall, when it touches the wall, then its sideways direction reverses and its speed is unchanged.

nodes.title: Each step a fish chooses a push as two numbers between −1 and 1 (left-right and up-down); its speed changes smoothly with the push, up to a top speed below the ball's.

criteria: Given a still fish pushing (1, 0) for several steps, when its speed is read, then it rises step by step toward its top speed, never above it.

nodes.title: When the ball touches a fish, the hit is counted and the fish reappears at a random spot at least one quarter of the tank's width from the ball.

criteria: Given the ball touching a fish, when the step ends, then the hit count is up by 1 and the fish is at least a quarter-width from the ball.

nodes.title: An episode lasts 1,000 steps; the score is hits per fish per episode (lower is better).

criteria: Given 4 fish and 6 total hits in an episode, when it ends, then the score is 1.5.

nodes.title: Variant "one fish": a single fish observes its own position and velocity and the ball's position and velocity.

criteria: Given the one-fish variant, when an observation is taken, then it holds those values for the fish and the ball.

nodes.title: Variant "many fish": 8 fish share the tank; each observes itself, the ball and the 3 nearest other fish.

criteria: Given the many-fish variant, when an observation is taken for any fish, then it holds its own state, the ball's and the 3 nearest fish's.

nodes.title: Variant "local sight": as "many fish", but a fish sees the ball and other fish only within a radius of one quarter of the tank's width; anything outside is reported as "not seen".

criteria: Given the ball beyond the radius, when a fish's observation is taken, then the ball's entries read "not seen".

nodes.title: Fish pass through each other; only the ball can hit them.

criteria: Given two fish moving onto the same spot, when the step ends, then both are there and no hit is counted.

nodes.title: The rule-based baseline pushes each fish directly away from the ball at full strength (from the ball it sees, or randomly when it sees none).

criteria: Given the ball to the fish's left, when the rule acts, then the push is (1, 0).

nodes.title: Every variant's trained fish beat both baselines as in EVAL-04 and EVAL-05.

criteria: Given 5 finished runs of each variant, when evaluated, then both baselines are beaten in each variant.

nodes.title: Fish tank runs through the same training runs, logging, replay viewer and evaluation as snake, and snake's results reproduce unchanged after fish tank is added.

criteria: Given a snake run repeated with its original settings and seed after fish tank exists, when it finishes, then its results match the original run exactly.

nodes.title: The arena is a square with walls, 6 prey, 2 predators and 10 food pellets; an eaten pellet reappears at a random spot after 50 steps.

criteria: Given seed 5, when an episode starts, then the counts are 6, 2 and 10, with no two objects touching.

nodes.title: Prey and predators move by smooth pushes as in FISH-02; predators' top speed is 1.2 × the prey's.

criteria: Given both at full speed, when their speeds are read, then the predator's is 1.2 × the prey's.

nodes.title: A prey touching a pellet eats it; a predator touching a prey catches it and the prey leaves the episode.

criteria: Given a predator touching a prey, when the step ends, then the prey is gone and the predator's catch count is up by 1.

nodes.title: An episode lasts 1,000 steps or until every prey is caught.

criteria: Given all 6 prey caught at step 600, when the step ends, then the episode is over.

nodes.title: Each team has its own score: prey score = pellets eaten per prey (higher is better); predator score = prey caught per episode (higher is better).

criteria: Given 18 pellets eaten and 3 prey caught, when the episode ends, then the prey score is 3 and the predator score is 3.

nodes.title: Every agent observes itself, and the nearest 2 food pellets, nearest 2 prey and nearest 2 predators within a radius of one third of the arena's width; anything outside reads "not seen".

criteria: Given a predator beyond the radius, when a prey's observation is taken, then that predator's entries read "not seen".

nodes.title: Rule-based baselines: prey flee the nearest seen predator, else move toward the nearest seen pellet; predators chase the nearest seen prey, else wander randomly.

criteria: Given a prey that sees a predator to its right, when the rule acts, then it pushes left.

nodes.title: Each trained team is evaluated against fixed opponents: trained prey against the rule-based predators, compared with random and rule-based prey; trained predators against the rule-based prey, compared with random and rule-based predators. Each passes as in EVAL-04 and EVAL-05.

criteria: Given 5 finished runs, when evaluated, then a separate verdict is shown for the prey team and the predator team.

nodes.title: The learner can play any prey checkpoint against any predator checkpoint from the same run, and see a grid of mean scores for every pairing of the 11 checkpoints of each side.

criteria: Given a finished run, when the pairing grid is made, then it shows an 11 × 11 grid of prey scores and of predator scores, each cell the mean of 20 held-out episodes.

nodes.title: The learning curve shows both teams' scores on the same step axis, so the back-and-forth between them is visible.

criteria: Given 5 finished runs, when the chart is made, then both teams' mean lines and bands appear against the same environment-steps axis.

nodes.title: Predator-prey runs through the same training runs, logging, replay viewer and evaluation as snake and fish tank, and their results reproduce unchanged after predator-prey is added.

criteria: Given a snake run and a fish run repeated with their original settings and seeds, when they finish, then their results match the originals exactly.

nodes.title: A single training run of any world and variant finishes within 60 minutes on the learner's laptop (Apple Silicon, CPU only).

criteria: Checked by the run's logged start and end times.

nodes.title: A batch of 5 runs of one world and variant finishes within 90 minutes on the same laptop, running in parallel.

criteria: Checked by the batch's first start and last end time.

nodes.title: Rented GPU time, if a world truly needs it, costs at most $10 per world, and is used only after a laptop run is shown to miss QR-01.

criteria: Checked against the rental bill, recorded in the world's write-up.

nodes.title: The replay viewer plays at least 30 steps per second at 1× on the laptop, for every world.

criteria: Checked by timing a 1,000-step replay.

nodes.title: Final evaluation (EVAL-03 and EVAL-04) of one world and variant finishes within 10 minutes on the laptop.

criteria: Checked by timing the evaluation.

nodes.title: Everything runs locally with no network connection once installed.

criteria: Checked by running a full train, evaluate and replay cycle with networking off.

nodes.title: In every world, a learning agent clearly beats both random play and a simple hand-written rule.
I can watch any trained agent play in a replay, and compare it with earlier points in training.
For every world, I can explain in my own words why its learning method works and where it struggles.
Each new world reuses one shared core (world interface, training loop, logging, replay viewer) instead of starting over.
A world starts a new episode from a seed, and the same seed always gives the same starting state.

criteria: Given a world and seed 42, when two episodes are started, then both starting states are identical.

nodes.title: Given the same seed and the same sequence of actions, a world produces the same sequence of observations, rewards and end signals.

criteria: Given a recorded episode's seed and actions, when they are replayed into a fresh world, then every observation, reward and end signal matches the recording.

nodes.title: Each agent's observation is a fixed-length list of numbers, never an image.

criteria: Given any world, when an observation is taken at any step, then it has the same length as at every other step of that world and variant.

nodes.title: A world declares its agents, the observation length and the action format (a choice from a fixed set, or a list of numbers within stated limits) before any episode starts.

criteria: Given any world, when the training loop asks for its description, then it receives the agent list, observation length and action format without running an episode.

nodes.title: Every world reports a per-episode score with a stated direction (higher is better, or lower is better), used by evaluation and charts.

criteria: Given a finished episode, when its score is requested, then a single number and the world's direction are returned.

nodes.title: A world reports its drawable state at every step (positions, sizes and kinds of every object) for the replay viewer.

criteria: Given any step of any episode, when the drawable state is requested, then every object on screen is listed with its position.

nodes.title: A world can hold more than one agent, each agent belonging to a named team.

criteria: Given a world with agents on two teams, when a step is taken, then each agent receives its own observation and reward, labelled with its team.

nodes.title: A training run is started from a world, a variant, the method's settings and a seed, and runs for a stated budget of environment steps.

criteria: Given snake, its default settings, seed 1 and a budget of N steps, when the run is started, then it stops after exactly N environment steps.

nodes.title: The same world, settings and seed on the same machine give an identical training run.

criteria: Given two runs with identical inputs, when both finish, then their logged results and final checkpoints are identical.

nodes.title: A run saves a checkpoint at every 10% of its budget, from the start (untrained) to the end.

criteria: Given a finished run, when its checkpoints are listed, then there are 11, at 0%, 10%, … 100% of the budget.

nodes.title: A run evaluates its current agent at every 5% of its budget on 20 episodes whose seeds are never used in training.

criteria: Given a finished run, when its evaluation log is read, then there are 21 evaluation points, each the mean score of 20 held-out-seed episodes.

nodes.title: Several runs of the same world with different seeds can be started together, one per processor core.

criteria: Given 5 seeds, when a batch of runs is started, then 5 runs proceed at the same time and each finishes with its own log and checkpoints.

nodes.title: Every learning method, before it is used in a world, learns the known best behavior in a tiny check world whose best behavior is worked out by hand.

criteria: Given a learning method and its check world, when it is trained for the check budget, then the trained agent picks the hand-derived best action in at least 95% of check-world states.

nodes.title: In worlds with more than one team, each team has its own learning method and settings, and all teams learn during the same run.

criteria: Given predator-prey with a learning method for each team, when a run proceeds, then both teams' agents change between consecutive checkpoints.

nodes.title: Every run records its world, variant, method settings, seed, budget, start and end times, and whether it finished.

criteria: Given any finished run, when its record is opened, then every one of those fields is present.

nodes.title: Every run logs, for each training episode, the episode's score, length and total reward per team.

criteria: Given a finished run, when its episode log is read, then it has one entry per training episode with those values.

nodes.title: For a world and variant with at least 3 finished runs, a learning-curve chart shows evaluation score against environment steps: the mean across runs as a line, the lowest-to-highest range across runs as a band, and each baseline's mean score as a horizontal reference line.

criteria: Given 5 finished snake runs, when the chart is made, then it shows one mean line, one band, a random-play line and a rule-based line, with the axes labelled with the score name and "environment steps".

nodes.title: Learning-curve charts follow the dataviz skill's guidance for form, colour and labelling.

criteria: Given any learning-curve chart, when it is reviewed against the dataviz skill, then it passes that skill's checks.

nodes.title: Each world can add its own logged measures (e.g. snake length at death, hits per fish), which are charted the same way as the score.

criteria: Given a world that declares an extra measure, when its chart is requested, then it is drawn with the same mean line and range band.

nodes.title: The learner can view the latest logged values of a run while it trains.

criteria: Given a run in progress, when the learner checks it, then they see the current step, the latest evaluation score and the time elapsed, no more than 1 evaluation point behind.

nodes.title: The learner can watch an episode played by any checkpoint of any run, from a seed they choose.

criteria: Given a snake run's 50% checkpoint and seed 7, when the replay is opened, then the episode plays from its first step to its end.

nodes.title: Replays are exact: the same checkpoint and seed always show the same episode.

criteria: Given a checkpoint and seed, when the replay is played twice, then every frame matches.

nodes.title: The replay can be paused, stepped one step forward or back, and played at 0.25×, 1×, 4× or 16× speed.

criteria: Given a paused replay at step 30, when the learner steps forward, then step 31 is shown; when they step back twice, step 29 is shown.

nodes.title: Two checkpoints can be shown side by side on the same starting state, stepping in sync.

criteria: Given the 10% and 100% snake checkpoints and seed 7, when compared, then both start from the same board and advance one step at a time together; when one episode ends, its last frame stays while the other continues.

nodes.title: The replay shows the current step, the running score and each agent's latest reward next to the world.

criteria: Given any frame, when it is shown, then the step number, the score so far and the latest rewards are visible.

nodes.title: The learner can also watch the random-play and rule-based baselines in the same viewer, including side by side with a checkpoint.

criteria: Given the rule-based snake and the final checkpoint on seed 7, when compared, then both play side by side as in REPLAY-04.

nodes.title: A replay can be saved as a video file to keep alongside the write-up.

criteria: Given an open replay, when the learner saves it, then a video of the whole episode at 1× speed is written and plays in a standard video player.

nodes.title: In worlds where agents see only nearby things, the replay can show each agent's sight radius as an overlay, switched on or off by the learner.

criteria: Given a local-sight fish replay, when the overlay is switched on, then a circle of the sight radius is drawn around every fish; when switched off, the circles disappear.

nodes.title: Every world and variant has a random-play baseline that picks each action uniformly from the allowed actions.

criteria: Given any world, when the random baseline plays 100 steps, then every action it takes is within the declared action format.

nodes.title: Every world and variant has a rule-based baseline that the learner writes by hand, described in one sentence in the world's feature below.

criteria: Given any world, when its rule baseline is listed, then its one-sentence description is shown with it.

nodes.title: Final evaluation plays every final checkpoint and both baselines on the same 100 seeds, none of which was used in training or in-training evaluation.

criteria: Given 5 finished runs, when final evaluation is run, then 700 episodes are played (5 × 100 learned, 100 random, 100 rule-based), all on the same 100 held-out seeds.

nodes.title: Whether the learned agent beats each baseline is tested with the null-hypothesis-testing skill. It is given: the hypothesis "the trained agent scores better than the baseline"; H0 = the learned agent's mean score is no better than the baseline's, H1 = it is better (in the world's score direction); the statistic = difference in mean episode score, learned (averaged over the runs, per seed) minus baseline; the null built by randomly swapping the learned and baseline labels within each held-out seed (paired permutation, 10,000 permutations); α = 0.05 with Holm correction across all baseline comparisons in that world (2 per variant); the EVAL-03 held-out episodes. The learned agent passes only if both nulls are rejected.

criteria: Given final evaluation results for one variant, when tested, then a report shows, for each baseline, the mean scores, the difference, the corrected p-value and reject/keep.

nodes.title: "Clearly beats" also needs every single run to beat the rule baseline: each run's final mean score is better than the rule-based baseline's mean score.

criteria: Given 5 runs where 4 beat the rule baseline and 1 does not, when the verdict is made, then the world is marked "not yet beating the baselines" and names the failing run.

nodes.title: Final evaluation produces one summary per world and variant: mean and range of learned scores across runs, both baseline means, the EVAL-04 test results and the EVAL-05 verdict.

criteria: Given a finished evaluation, when the summary is opened, then all of those values are present.

nodes.title: The learning algorithms (how actions are chosen, what is learned from each experience, and how the agent is updated) are written by the learner; automatic gradient computation may be used, but an established reference implementation of a learning method is used only for this check, never inside training runs.

criteria: Given any training run, when it runs, then no outside reinforcement-learning code takes part in it.

nodes.title: For each world and variant, 5 runs of a reference implementation of the same kind of method are trained on the same world, budget and seeds as the hand-written method, and evaluated as in EVAL-03.

criteria: Given a finished reference check, when its summary is opened, then it shows the reference's mean and range next to the hand-written method's.

nodes.title: The hand-written method passes the check if its mean final score is at least 80% of the reference's (or at most 125% for lower-is-better scores).

criteria: Given a hand-written snake mean of 18 food and a reference mean of 20, when checked, then it passes; at 15 against 20, it is flagged for investigation.

nodes.title: Each world has a write-up with three parts: how the learning method works, why it works in this world, and where it struggles.

criteria: Given a finished world, when its write-up is opened, then all three parts are present and non-empty.

nodes.title: The "where it struggles" part points to at least one saved replay or chart that shows the struggle.

criteria: Given a write-up, when its struggle part is read, then it names at least one saved replay or chart that exists.

nodes.title: Write-ups are the learner's own words; nothing in the system writes or fills them in.

criteria: Given a new world, when it is set up, then its write-up starts with only the three part headings.

nodes.title: The world is a 10 × 10 grid with one snake starting 3 cells long in the middle, and one food item on a random free cell.

criteria: Given seed 3, when an episode starts, then the snake is 3 cells long near the center and one food item is on a cell the snake does not cover.

nodes.title: Each step the snake chooses one of three actions: turn left, turn right or go straight.

criteria: Given the snake heading up, when it turns left, then its head moves one cell left.

nodes.title: Eating food grows the snake by one cell, adds 1 to the score and places new food on a random free cell.

criteria: Given the head moves onto food, when the step ends, then the snake is one cell longer, the score is up by 1 and new food is on a free cell.

nodes.title: The episode ends when the head hits a wall or the snake's body, or after 100 steps without eating.

criteria: Given the head moves into its own body, when the step ends, then the episode is over.

nodes.title: The score is the food eaten in the episode (higher is better).

criteria: Given an episode where 12 food items were eaten, when it ends, then its score is 12.

nodes.title: The snake observes a fixed list of numbers: danger straight ahead, left and right; its heading; the food's direction relative to its head; and its length.

criteria: Given any step, when the observation is taken, then it has the same length and holds those values.

nodes.title: The rule-based baseline moves toward the food along the shorter axis, unless that move would end the episode next step, in which case it takes any move that does not.

criteria: Given the food to the right and a free cell to the right, when the rule acts, then it moves right.

nodes.title: The trained snake beats both baselines as in EVAL-04 and EVAL-05.

criteria: Given 5 finished snake runs, when evaluated, then both baselines are beaten.

nodes.title: The tank is a square with walls; the ball moves in straight lines at constant speed and bounces off walls.

criteria: Given the ball heading into the right wall, when it touches the wall, then its sideways direction reverses and its speed is unchanged.

nodes.title: Each step a fish chooses a push as two numbers between −1 and 1 (left-right and up-down); its speed changes smoothly with the push, up to a top speed below the ball's.

criteria: Given a still fish pushing (1, 0) for several steps, when its speed is read, then it rises step by step toward its top speed, never above it.

nodes.title: When the ball touches a fish, the hit is counted and the fish reappears at a random spot at least one quarter of the tank's width from the ball.

criteria: Given the ball touching a fish, when the step ends, then the hit count is up by 1 and the fish is at least a quarter-width from the ball.

nodes.title: An episode lasts 1,000 steps; the score is hits per fish per episode (lower is better).

criteria: Given 4 fish and 6 total hits in an episode, when it ends, then the score is 1.5.

nodes.title: Variant "one fish": a single fish observes its own position and velocity and the ball's position and velocity.

criteria: Given the one-fish variant, when an observation is taken, then it holds those values for the fish and the ball.

nodes.title: Variant "many fish": 8 fish share the tank; each observes itself, the ball and the 3 nearest other fish.

criteria: Given the many-fish variant, when an observation is taken for any fish, then it holds its own state, the ball's and the 3 nearest fish's.

nodes.title: Variant "local sight": as "many fish", but a fish sees the ball and other fish only within a radius of one quarter of the tank's width; anything outside is reported as "not seen".

criteria: Given the ball beyond the radius, when a fish's observation is taken, then the ball's entries read "not seen".

nodes.title: Fish pass through each other; only the ball can hit them.

criteria: Given two fish moving onto the same spot, when the step ends, then both are there and no hit is counted.

nodes.title: The rule-based baseline pushes each fish directly away from the ball at full strength (from the ball it sees, or randomly when it sees none).

criteria: Given the ball to the fish's left, when the rule acts, then the push is (1, 0).

nodes.title: Every variant's trained fish beat both baselines as in EVAL-04 and EVAL-05.

criteria: Given 5 finished runs of each variant, when evaluated, then both baselines are beaten in each variant.

nodes.title: Fish tank runs through the same training runs, logging, replay viewer and evaluation as snake, and snake's results reproduce unchanged after fish tank is added.

criteria: Given a snake run repeated with its original settings and seed after fish tank exists, when it finishes, then its results match the original run exactly.

nodes.title: The arena is a square with walls, 6 prey, 2 predators and 10 food pellets; an eaten pellet reappears at a random spot after 50 steps.

criteria: Given seed 5, when an episode starts, then the counts are 6, 2 and 10, with no two objects touching.

nodes.title: Prey and predators move by smooth pushes as in FISH-02; predators' top speed is 1.2 × the prey's.

criteria: Given both at full speed, when their speeds are read, then the predator's is 1.2 × the prey's.

nodes.title: A prey touching a pellet eats it; a predator touching a prey catches it and the prey leaves the episode.

criteria: Given a predator touching a prey, when the step ends, then the prey is gone and the predator's catch count is up by 1.

nodes.title: An episode lasts 1,000 steps or until every prey is caught.

criteria: Given all 6 prey caught at step 600, when the step ends, then the episode is over.

nodes.title: Each team has its own score: prey score = pellets eaten per prey (higher is better); predator score = prey caught per episode (higher is better).

criteria: Given 18 pellets eaten and 3 prey caught, when the episode ends, then the prey score is 3 and the predator score is 3.

nodes.title: Every agent observes itself, and the nearest 2 food pellets, nearest 2 prey and nearest 2 predators within a radius of one third of the arena's width; anything outside reads "not seen".

criteria: Given a predator beyond the radius, when a prey's observation is taken, then that predator's entries read "not seen".

nodes.title: Rule-based baselines: prey flee the nearest seen predator, else move toward the nearest seen pellet; predators chase the nearest seen prey, else wander randomly.

criteria: Given a prey that sees a predator to its right, when the rule acts, then it pushes left.

nodes.title: Each trained team is evaluated against fixed opponents: trained prey against the rule-based predators, compared with random and rule-based prey; trained predators against the rule-based prey, compared with random and rule-based predators. Each passes as in EVAL-04 and EVAL-05.

criteria: Given 5 finished runs, when evaluated, then a separate verdict is shown for the prey team and the predator team.

nodes.title: The learner can play any prey checkpoint against any predator checkpoint from the same run, and see a grid of mean scores for every pairing of the 11 checkpoints of each side.

criteria: Given a finished run, when the pairing grid is made, then it shows an 11 × 11 grid of prey scores and of predator scores, each cell the mean of 20 held-out episodes.

nodes.title: The learning curve shows both teams' scores on the same step axis, so the back-and-forth between them is visible.

criteria: Given 5 finished runs, when the chart is made, then both teams' mean lines and bands appear against the same environment-steps axis.

nodes.title: Predator-prey runs through the same training runs, logging, replay viewer and evaluation as snake and fish tank, and their results reproduce unchanged after predator-prey is added.

criteria: Given a snake run and a fish run repeated with their original settings and seeds, when they finish, then their results match the originals exactly.

nodes.title: A single training run of any world and variant finishes within 60 minutes on the learner's laptop (Apple Silicon, CPU only).

criteria: Checked by the run's logged start and end times.

nodes.title: A batch of 5 runs of one world and variant finishes within 90 minutes on the same laptop, running in parallel.

criteria: Checked by the batch's first start and last end time.

nodes.title: Rented GPU time, if a world truly needs it, costs at most $10 per world, and is used only after a laptop run is shown to miss QR-01.

criteria: Checked against the rental bill, recorded in the world's write-up.

nodes.title: The replay viewer plays at least 30 steps per second at 1× on the laptop, for every world.

criteria: Checked by timing a 1,000-step replay.

nodes.title: Final evaluation (EVAL-03 and EVAL-04) of one world and variant finishes within 10 minutes on the laptop.

criteria: Checked by timing the evaluation.

nodes.title: Everything runs locally with no network connection once installed.

criteria: Checked by running a full train, evaluate and replay cycle with networking off.
